entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: mcp__scheduled-tasks__create_scheduled_task
entries.description:
Create a scheduled task that runs automatically — on a recurring schedule or once at a future moment. Use this when the user asks for something to happen repeatedly ("every day at 6am", "each Monday", "hourly") or at a specific later time ("remind me in 20 minutes", "tomorrow at 3pm"), rather than once right now. Go ahead and call it when the request clearly describes a schedule; if the schedule or task content is ambiguous, confirm the details with the user first — an approval prompt may or may not appear depending on the user's permission settings, so don't rely on it as the confirmation step.

To modify an existing scheduled task's schedule or prompt, use `update_scheduled_task` instead.

The task is stored as {taskId}/SKILL.md in C:\Users\edmem\.claude\scheduled-tasks/. Each run starts fresh with no memory of this conversation, so the prompt must be fully self-contained: include which connectors to use, the output format, and any preferences the user expressed here.

Scheduled tasks run while this app is open. If the app is closed when a task is due, it runs on next launch — tell the user this so they aren't surprised.

**Scheduling options (pick at most one):**
- cronExpression: recurring (daily, weekly, etc.)
- fireAt: one-time — runs once at the given moment, then auto-disables. Never use a cron expression for a one-time task; cron has no one-shot semantics.
- Omit both: "ad-hoc" — can only be started manually

**Recurring (cronExpression):** Cron is evaluated in the user's LOCAL timezone, not UTC. Use local times directly. Format: minute hour dayOfMonth month dayOfWeek
- "0 9 * * *" — Every day at 9:00 AM local time
- "0 9 * * 1-5" — Weekdays at 9:00 AM local time
- "30 8 * * 1" — Every Monday at 8:30 AM local time
- "0 0 1 * *" — First day of every month at midnight local time

**One-time (fireAt):** An ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone offset. The task fires once at that moment (or on next app launch if it was closed), then disables itself.
- "2026-03-05T14:30:00-08:00" — Runs once on March 5 at 2:30 PM … [truncated]

11219 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

1. **Split `resolveDownloadUrl` into a sync half (`resolveDownloadUrlSync`) and the network half.**
   spigotmc/steam_workshop/mod_io/github/etc. never needed a network call to begin with (spigotmc builds
   its Spiget URL synchronously; everything else just returns `mod.url`) — only modrinth/thunderstore do.
   `resolveDownloadUrlSync` returns immediately for every source except those two, and returns
   `undefined` (meaning "needs a live call") for them.
2. **StoreBrowser's grid now calls `resolveDownloadUrlSync` (0 network calls) instead of
   `resolveDownloadUrl` (up to 24 concurrent network calls) for every page render.** For the
   Modrinth/Thunderstore rows it can't resolve synchronously, it renders the new `DownloadButton` client
   component instead of a plain `<a>` — a click-to-resolve button that calls a new server action
   (`resolveModDownloadAction`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`) which runs the exact same `resolveDownloadUrl`
   function, but only for the ONE mod actually clicked, only when it's clicked. The mod detail pages
   (`app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`)
   are untouched — they already only ever resolved one mod and keep doing exactly that.
3. **Added a 5-second timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`) to both live fetch calls inside
   `resolveDownloadUrl`.** There was no timeout at all before — this bounds the worst case for the
   single-mod detail-page/click-resolve call path, which had no cap before this fix.
4. **Added the 3 composite indexes `EXPLAIN` showed were missing**, to `GameMod` in
   `prisma/schema.prisma`: `(featured DESC, downloads DESC, popularity DESC, name)`,
   `(downloads DESC, name)`, `(createdAt DESC)` — matching `queryCatalogMods`'s real `ORDER_BY` shapes.
   Verified the fix live WITHOUT touching production schema: created each index inside a Postgres
   transaction against real production data, ran `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, then rolled back (0 indexes left
   behind, confirmed by re-querying `pg_indexes` after). Real before/after, same production data:
   featured sort **69.6ms → 0.099ms**, downloads sort **62.3ms → 0.082ms**, minecraft-family featured
   sort **68.2ms → 0.112ms** — Seq Scan + top-N heapsort became an Index Scan in every case, the same
   technique the existing `upstreamUpdatedAt` index already proved (a plain index on the sort column is
   enough; Postgres still applies `active`/`upstreamOk` as a cheap Filter during the index scan, no
   partial/filtered index needed — which Prisma's schema DSL can't express anyway). This is real,
   additive, forward-looking hardening (safe at today's 46MB table size regardless) rather than the
   actual fix for the reported symptom, per the measurements above. **Not yet applied to any database**
   — `prisma db push` was NOT run against `nxeon` or `nxeon_staging`; the schema change ships with the
   next real deploy the same way every other schema change in this repo does.
5. **Cached `listCatalogFamilies` and `totalDownloadsFor`** with `unstable_cache` (10-minute revalidate)
   — both were already cheap (24-30ms) so this isn't the fix for the reported symptom either, but it
   removes real repeated DB round trips under concurrent traffic for two aggregates that only change via
   periodic backfill scripts, never a live user action.

**Real before/after (production data, this session, via `scripts/_tmp-resolve-download-perf*.ts`,
`scripts/_tmp-resolve-download-after.ts`, deleted after use per convention):**

| Page (default sort, page 1) | Before (`resolveDownloadUrl` in the grid) | After (`resolveDownloadUrlSync` in the grid) |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-game `/mods` (7 of 24 mods are Modrinth) | 2079ms | 0ms (7 deferred to click-resolve) |
| `/mods/games/minecraft` (22 of 24 mods are Modrinth) | 2183ms | 0ms (22 deferred to click-resolve) |
| `/mods/games/minecraft?sort=downloads` | 2073ms | 0ms (22 deferred to click-resolve) |

Direct `curl` against the live production server before this fix: `/mods` 2.56-4.03s,
`/mods/games/minecraft` 2.60-3.51s (3 requests each). **The code fix above was NOT deployed to
production this session** (this task's process intentionally stops short of running
`deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` — the owner deploys after review), so a live post-fix `curl`
number does not yet exist; the ~2.0-2.2s removed from the render's critical path is the measured,
verified reduction, not a projection.

**Files touched:** `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`, `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`,
`components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `components/mods/DownloadButton.tsx` (new), `prisma/schema.prisma`.

I actually do call escAttr on the `[url=]` and `[url]` handlers already — only the `[img]` handler is missing it with its unescaped src attribute. But the reviewer flagged escAttr usage here as potentially double-encoding-prone since the text already passed through the outer esc(bbcode) call, so I want to re-check their finding more carefully.

Their finding #4 specifically calls out `[img]` at line 323 as attribute injection, matching what I see — no escAttr at all there. The "double encoding" note is a separate caveat about the href lines (335/340), where calling escAttr again on already-escaped text could turn `&` into `&amp;` — a correctness bug from over-escaping, not an actual security hole, since over-escaping is safe just ugly. So my real conclusion is that lines 335/340 are safe but garbled by double-encoding, while the img src line is the genuine XSS risk from missing escAttr entirely.

Since security matters most, I'll fix the missing escAttr at the img line first as critical, then address the double-encoding on the href lines by introducing a quote-only escape helper for contexts where text has already passed through the main escape once, fixing both problems in a single pass.

Now I'm double-checking whether safeImageSrc/safeLinkHref could let raw `<`/`>` characters slip through unescaped, since they only validate the URL scheme prefix and otherwise return the string untouched.

In already-escaped contexts, any `<`/`>` would already be safe entities from the prior `esc()` pass, while in the raw standalone-image-line case, `escAttr`'s internal `esc()` call still catches them—so my plan holds. I'm also considering whether an attacker could type literal `"` as raw text before escaping, which would need separate handling.

Since `esc()` only touches `&`, `<`, `>`, a literal `&` in `"` always becomes `&quot;`, never a real quote-entity, so there's no way for attacker-forged sequences to slip through post-escaping—confirming the quote-only escape is sufficient without extra safeguards.

Now I'm planning the actual fixes: adding a helper to escape quotes on already-escaped text, then applying it to the `src` and `href` attributes in the image and link handling within `inlineMd`.

Since fully fixing the unmatched closing tag issue would require stateful stack-based tracking of opening/closing tags, and this is more of a content-integrity issue than a security one, I'll document it as a known low-severity limitation instead of building the full fix now — a reasonable scoping tradeoff given everything else that needs addressing.

The code-span-inside-URL edge case results in broken markup that degrades to plain text rather than becoming an exploitable attribute, so it's confirmed non-exploitable and rare enough to leave unfixed. Time to apply the fixes.

Root cause was per-importer, already diagnosed by the audit; this session implemented every fix, verified each against real upstream/production data, and ran the one action the audit's own scoped fix plan called for against production: the Modrinth description backfill. Done on the isolated worktree `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc` (branch `fix/nxlabs-mod-descriptions`) — **the code changes below are NOT committed/pushed/deployed**; only the data backfill (below) ran against production, from `/opt/nxeon` directly, using the pre-existing, unmodified `scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts`. **1. Slug-decode 404 fix (`lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s `getCatalogMod`).** 377 mod detail pages 404'd for slugs containing `+`, `,`, `` ` ``, `"` (real, unsanitized Modrinth project slugs — e.g. `abyss+`, `0,5-hp`, `"limitless"-banners`). Root cause, confirmed by direct investigation (the audit named the right symptom but the actual mechanism took a live repro to pin down): for a `page.tsx` route that also exports `generateStaticParams`, this Next.js version hands the page's dynamic segment `params` value as the STILL-PERCENT-ENCODED raw path segment — e.g. requesting `/mods/minecraft/abyss+` makes `params.slug` arrive as the literal string `"abyss%2B"`, not `"abyss+"` — confirmed by a temporary debug route (removed before finishing) that showed a plain Route Handler on the identical path shape decodes normally, isolating the bug to the `generateStaticParams` + page.tsx combination specifically. Fixed by decoding (with a raw-value fallback for the rare literal `%` in a slug) inside `getCatalogMod` itself, so both callers (public `/mods/[family]/[slug]` and portal `/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]`) get the fix from one place. **Verified live** (local dev server against the real production DB): all 4 previously-404 sample URLs now return 200 with correct titles; a DB count of `slug ~ '[+,\`"]'` confirms exactly 377 mods were affected. **2. New renderer, `lib/mod-markdown.ts`** (NOT `lib/blog.ts`'s `renderMarkdown`, which stays first-party -only — blog/admin-docs/announcements keep their simple "escape everything" model). Real Modrinth bodies routinely embed raw HTML (`
`, ``, `
`, `
`, real `

`/`

`/`
    `/`
  • ` used directly instead of markdown syntax — all confirmed live) which the old renderer turned into visible literal escaped tag text. Safety model: escape everything first, then selectively restore a fixed allow-list of tags by matching the ALREADY-ESCAPED text — an arbitrary string can't forge its way back to a real tag unless it exactly matches one of the fixed patterns, and `src`/`href` values are extracted, revalidated (https-only for images; http(s)/root-relative-only for links; `javascript:`/`data:`/ protocol-relative rejected), and re-emitted through a fresh template, never echoed verbatim. Also: every in-body heading (markdown `#`-`######`, BBCode `[h1]`-`[h3]`) is capped at `

    ` so a mod author can never inject a second page `

    `/`

    `; truncation (still 6,000 chars) now cuts at a real paragraph/line boundary in the raw SOURCE before rendering, never mid-tag; a "Read the full description on X →" link appears when truncated. Steam Workshop's real BBCode gets its own `renderBBCode` (square brackets aren't HTML-meaningful, so the same escape-then-restore approach applies). **Two real bugs found and fixed by an adversarial security review before any of this was considered done** (both independently reproduced and re-verified fixed with the exact repro strings below): - **Stored XSS via attribute break-out.** Four spots (markdown standalone/inline image, markdown inline link, BBCode `[img]`) embedded a URL into `src="..."`/`href="..."` WITHOUT escaping it — `safeImageSrc`/ `safeLinkHref` only validate the URL's scheme, they don't neutralize a literal `"` inside it. A crafted mod body like `![a](https://x.png">INJECTED)` broke out of the attribute and injected real markup into every visitor's DOM. Fixed by wrapping every embedded URL/alt-text in `escAttr` (raw-text contexts) or a new `escAttrPostEscaped` helper (contexts already run through `esc()` once — using full `escAttr` there would double-encode a real `&` in a legitimate CDN query string, e.g. `?w=200&h=100`, into `&`). **Verified**: all 5 of the reviewer's repro strings now render fully quoted/escaped, no raw break-out; a legit `?w=200&h=100` URL now round-trips as a single `&`. - **ReDoS.** The original `restoreSafeHtml` regexes chained several adjustable-length pieces against the same character class (e.g. `\s+([^&]*?)\/?\s*>`) — on adversarial input with no closing `>` (trivial to publish: `` with no opener) can prematurely close one of THIS renderer's own wrapper tags, visually breaking layout within the card — it cannot escape the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` fragment to reach real page chrome (confirmed: React's fragment-parsing can't let inner content close an ancestor outside the fragment being parsed), so this is a content-integrity nuisance, not a security hole. A full stack-based well-formedness pass would close this; not built this pass. - **Separate, pre-existing, out-of-scope finding from the same review** (flagged via `spawn_task`, not fixed here): the marketing mod-detail page's JSON-LD `` sequences — a mod named to contain `` could end that script tag early. Untouched by this session's diff. **3. Modrinth (`scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`, `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`).** The bulk `/v2/projects?ids=[...]` call already returned `body` (thousands of real chars per project — confirmed live) but `FullProject`'s type never declared it, so it was silently dropped even after being fetched. Added `body`/`categories` to the type; `categories` declared but NOT wired into the upsert — `GameMod .category` is a single string tied to an existing, live filter-chip vocabulary (Admin/Economy/Performance/ ...) that all 32,243 Modrinth rows already populate with the project-type label; overwriting it with Modrinth's own, differently-shaped category facet needs a real schema/UI decision, not a silent swap — flagged as a follow-up rather than guessed at. `longDescription: full?.body?.trim() || null` added to the upsert. Same `body` capture added to `verify-gamemods.ts`'s `verifyModrinth()` (it already called `/v2/project/{id}`, which also carries `body`, and was discarding it the same way). **4. Steam Workshop (`scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`).** `return_short_description=true` (dropped) was truncating every item's real BBCode `file_description` to 256 chars server-side before the script ever saw it (verified live against every one of the 8,950 live rows: max AND median description length exactly 256 — Steam's own truncation, not a schema constraint, the column is unbounded text). Added `return_previews`/`return_tags` (both confirmed live to return real data once requested — `tags` now maps to `category` via a best-effort ruleset, `previews` — image type only, sorted by the source's own `sortorder` — populates `galleryUrls`) and `return_children` (parsed but not consumed yet — no `dependencyCount` field exists to fill from Workshop's children list; left for a follow-up, consistent with Modrinth/Thunderstore's own importers not chasing dependency data from their bulk endpoints either). `file_size` (already present in every response regardless of flags) now populates `fileBytes`. The short `description` tagline is now derived from `file_description` (BBCode-stripped to plain text, word-boundary truncated) since the response no longer carries a separate truncated field. **5. Thunderstore (`scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`, `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`).** The v1 catalogue this script already fetches has no body field beyond the manifest's short `description` (<=250 chars) — the real README lives at the experimental per-package, per-version endpoint (verified live: BepInExPack_Valheim's README is 8,237 chars of real markdown), one request per package, no bulk form. Added a sequential, self-paced (120/min, no documented Thunderstore limit exists to honor — this is a self-imposed "polite citizen" pace) README-fetch pass that runs to completion BEFORE the existing concurrent DB-write loop (a shared rate limiter doesn't serialize correctly across concurrent callers, so mixing the two would let request bursts through). Also captured `file_size` (real, present per-version in the v1 catalogue, confirmed live: BepInExPack_Valheim's latest version is 702,924 bytes) into `fileBytes` — previously always written `null`. Fixed the matching bug in `verify-gamemods.ts`'s `verifyThunderstore()`: it unconditionally overwrote `fileBytes`/`galleryUrls` back to `null`/`[]` on every scheduled run (its endpoint has neither field), silently erasing what the import script had just written; `VerifyResult`'s `fileBytes`/`galleryUrls`/(new)`longDescription` are now OPTIONAL — present = write it, omitted = "no fresher signal, leave the stored value alone" (Prisma treats an `undefined` data field as "not provided"). `verifyThunderstore()` now also fetches the README itself for ongoing freshness. **6. uMod (`scripts/import-umod-catalog.ts`, new).** `verify-gamemods.ts` wrongly claimed uMod has no public API (fixed, see below) — it does: `umod.org/plugins/search.json`, paged, keyless, real (confirmed live: 1,710 total listed items, ~83% tagged `rust` in a spot-check across pages 1/20/50/90/130/171, consistent with the audit's ~1,419-plugin estimate against the 29 hand-seeded rows that existed before this). **NOT run against production, and deliberately scoped to metadata-only, no per-plugin fetches, no file mirroring**: `umod.org`'s own ToS page and `robots.txt` are both behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (confirmed live: both return HTTP 403 "Just a moment..."), so this session could not actually read uMod's terms before writing an importer against it. A human should confirm the real ToS (through a real browser) before this is ever run with `--apply` against production — flagged explicitly in the script's own file header. Separately confirmed live: even the per-plugin JSON (`/plugins/.json`) has no field longer than the short `description` — there is no Modrinth-`body`-equivalent to fetch here even once ToS is clear, so this script can close the "only 29 of 1,419 Rust plugins imported" gap but can't move uMod's own 0%-of-`longDescription` number the way the other three sources' fixes do. **7. Weekly refresh — `deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.{timer,service}` + `scripts/weekly-mod-catalog- refresh.sh`, following the exact `deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.*` pattern already used for the nightly Improvements scanner** (systemd `Type=oneshot` timer pair; oneshot itself is the concurrency guard — systemd refuses to start an already-running oneshot again). Nothing had re-run any importer or `verify-gamemods.ts` on any schedule at all (checked: no timer, no crontab, no worker job) — every one of the 45,761 rows was last touched the day the original bulk imports ran. Re-runs Modrinth, Steam Workshop, and Thunderstore importers with `--apply`, then `verify-gamemods.ts`, in that order, once a week (Monday 03:15). Deliberately does NOT include `import-umod-catalog.ts` — see point 6. Not yet installed (`sudo systemctl enable --now nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.timer` — see `deploy/WEEKLY-MODCATALOG-README.md`). **Real before/after, production data, this session (`GameMod`, `active AND upstreamOk`, 45,761 rows):** | Source | Total | `longDescription` before | `longDescription` after | |---|---|---|---| | modrinth | 32,243 | 0 (0.0%) | **31,842 (98.8%)** | | steam_workshop | 8,950 | 0 | 0 *(code fixed, not re-imported against prod this session)* | | mod_io | 2,725 | 2,314 (84.9%) | 2,314 (unchanged — already working) | | thunderstore | 1,771 | 0 | 0 *(code fixed, not re-imported against prod this session)* | | umod / github / nexus / spigotmc / codefling | 72 | 0 | 0 *(umod code written, not run — ToS; others out of scope)* | | **catalogue-wide** | **45,761** | **2,314 (5.1%)** | **34,156 (74.6%)** | The Modrinth backfill (`scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts`, written 2026-09-20, never run before this session) ran against production in three steps, per its own safety instructions: a 50-row dry run (`--limit=50`), then the same 50 rows for real (`--limit=50 --apply`) with the rendered output eyeballed on real pages (`bookshelf-lib`, `no-chat-reports`, `owo-lib`, `create-fabric` — including a specific check for `
    `/`
    `/`` raw-HTML handling), then the full remaining 32,193-row run. Final: checked=31,793 (the 50 already done), filled=31,771, empty_body=1 (a project with a genuinely empty body — left null, not padded), missing_from_api=21 (renamed/removed projects), failed=400 (4 whole 100-row batches hit a consistent — re-run, same 4 batches failed identically, not a transient 429/5xx — HTTP 400; root cause not fully chased down this session, plausibly the encoded-URL-length limit on a `GET .../projects?ids=[...]` batch of 100 slugs when several are long; left as a small, ~1.2%-of-catalogue follow-up, not blocking since the script is idempotent and safe to re-run with a fix later). **What ran against production vs what's staged for review:** ONLY the Modrinth description backfill (`backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts`, unmodified by this session) ran against `nxeon` — a real, one-directional, additive data fill (`longDescription IS NULL` rows only), using a script whose own file header already documents it as safe/idempotent/non-fabricating. Every CODE change (the renderer, the slug-decode fix, all import/verify script fixes, the new uMod importer, the weekly timer) is uncommitted on the isolated worktree `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc` (branch `fix/nxlabs-mod-descriptions`) — not committed, not pushed (this repo's post-commit hook auto-pushes, so committing would have pushed it), not deployed to staging or production. A human should review the diff, then either promote it through the normal `deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `promote-production.sh` pipeline, or ask for it to be committed/ pushed first. **Files touched (code, staged for review):** `lib/mod-markdown.ts` (new), `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-umod-catalog.ts` (new), `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`, `scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh` (new), `deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.timer` (new), `deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.service` (new), `deploy/WEEKLY-MODCATALOG-README.md` (new). **Data touched (ran against production):** `GameMod .longDescription` for 31,842 modrinth rows. --- *Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (server migration).*

input.title: Fix JSON-LD script-injection in mod detail page
input.prompt:
In /opt/nxeon (Nxeon platform repo), the file `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx` (around lines 219-247, may have shifted slightly if other edits landed first — search for `type="application/ld+json"` in that file) renders a JSON-LD structured-data `<script>` tag via:

```tsx
<script
  type="application/ld+json"
  dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
    __html: JSON.stringify({
      "@context": "https://schema.org",
      "@type": "SoftwareApplication",
      name: mod.name,
      description: mod.description || `${mod.name} for ${mod.gameFamilyLabel}.`,
      ...(mod.authorName ? { author: { "@type": "Person", name: mod.authorName } } : {}),
      // ... more fields
    }),
  }}
/>
```

`mod.name`, `mod.description`, and `mod.authorName` are ALL genuinely third-party, attacker-influenced text — they come from the live NxLabs mod catalog (Modrinth/Steam Workshop/Thunderstore/uMod project titles, descriptions, and author names, imported by scripts under `scripts/import-*-catalog.ts`). `JSON.stringify` does NOT escape `<` or `/`, so a mod published upstream with a name/description/author containing the literal substring `</script>` (e.g. a project named `Foo</script><script>alert(1)</script>`) would have that string appear verbatim inside this inline `<script>` block. Since this is embedded via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` into real HTML, the browser's HTML PARSER (not the JSON parser) sees `</script>` first and terminates the script tag early, letting whatever follows be parsed as live HTML/script — a real, classic JSON-LD script-injection XSS. This is exploitable by anyone who can publish a project to Modrinth/Steam Workshop/etc. with a crafted name — no special access to Nxeon needed, since the import scripts pull this text automatically.

Context: this was found in passing during an adversarial security review of a NEW file (`lib/mod-markdown.ts`) built in a separate, still-uncommitted piece of work (worktree `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc`, branch `fix/nxlabs-mod-descriptions` — not related to this bug, that work is about rendering mod DESCRIPTIONS safely, this bug is in the surrounding page's JSON-LD block, pre-existing, untouched by that work). This ticket is standalone and doesn't depend on that other branch landing first.

There's already a shared, safe pattern in the codebase for simple cases: `components/marketing/StructuredData.tsx` renders `<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(data) }} />` too, with a comment saying "JSON.stringify output is safe to inline; no user input here" — that assumption is exactly what's violated on the mod detail page, which is why it doesn't use that shared component and instead builds its own inline block.

Fix: escape `<` (and ideally `>` and `&` for belt-and-suspenders, though `<` is the actual exploit vector for closing `</script>`) in the JSON.stringify output before inlining it — the standard fix is `JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")` (or replace all three of `<`, `>`, `&` if being thorough — many real-world implementations, e.g. Next.js's own internal script serialization, do exactly this). Apply the same audit to check whether ANY other JSON-LD block in this codebase embeds third-party/user-generated content the same way — grep for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML.*JSON.stringify` across `app/` (there are a handful of other files using the pattern, e.g. `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/tools/minecraft-server-status/page.tsx` — check each one for whether any field it serializes is genuinely third-party/attacker-controlled vs. first-party/developer-controlled; only the ones with real third-party content need the fix, don't change ones that only ever carry static/first-party data). Consider adding the escape to the shared `StructuredData.tsx` helper too as defense-in-depth, and updating its "no user input here" comment if you change its guarantee.

Typecheck (`npx tsc --noEmit`) and confirm the fix with a quick repro: render a mod (or synthetic data) whose name contains `</script><script>alert(1)</script>` and confirm the output no longer contains a literal `</script>` substring inside the JSON-LD block.
input.tldr: While reviewing a new sanitizing renderer for mod descriptions, an adversarial security check found that the mod detail page's JSON-LD block inlines third-party mod name/description/author text via JSON.stringify without escaping `</script>`, letting a maliciously-named upstream mod break out of the script tag and inject real markup. This spins off a fix for that separate, pre-existing bug.

## Summary Worked in an isolated worktree (`/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc`, branch `fix/nxlabs-mod-descriptions`) per the task's isolation requirement, and verified every audit claim against the current code and real upstream APIs before changing anything (several turned out subtly different from how the audit described them — see below). **What I fixed, per source:** 1. **Slug-decode 404s (`lib/mods-catalog.ts`)** — root-caused precisely via a live repro (added a temporary debug route, since removed): for a `page.tsx` with `generateStaticParams`, this Next.js version hands `params.slug` back **still percent-encoded** (`"abyss%2B"`, not `"abyss+"`) — a plain Route Handler on the identical path decodes correctly, so it's specific to that combination. Fixed by decoding inside `getCatalogMod` itself (with a raw-value fallback). Verified live: all 4 sample 404 URLs now return 200 with correct titles; confirmed exactly 377 mods were affected. 2. **New renderer, `lib/mod-markdown.ts`** — escape-first/allow-list-restore renderer replacing `lib/blog.ts`'s renderer for mod bodies only. Handles raw HTML (`
`, `
`, real `

`/`

`/`
    `/`
  • ` used directly — all confirmed live in real Modrinth bodies), caps in-body headings at `

    `, truncates at a real paragraph boundary, and gives Steam Workshop its own BBCode renderer. 3. **Modrinth** — added `body`/`categories` to `FullProject`, wired `longDescription` into the upsert and into `verify-gamemods.ts`'s `verifyModrinth()`. `categories` deliberately not wired into the upsert (would silently repurpose a live filter-chip field) — flagged as a follow-up. 4. **Steam Workshop** — dropped `return_short_description` (confirmed live it truncates to exactly 256 chars), added `return_previews`/`return_tags`, wired `file_size`→`fileBytes`, `previews`→`galleryUrls`, `tags`→`category`. 5. **Thunderstore** — added a rate-limited README-fetch pass (real per-package endpoint, confirmed live) into `longDescription`, captured real `file_size`→`fileBytes` from the v1 catalogue, and fixed `verify-gamemods.ts`'s `verifyThunderstore()` which was **silently nulling `fileBytes`/`galleryUrls` on every scheduled run** — made those fields optional so "no fresher data" means "don't touch," not "erase." 6. **uMod (`scripts/import-umod-catalog.ts`, new)** — real API confirmed (`umod.org/plugins/search.json`, ~1,419 Rust plugins). **Not run against prod**: uMod's ToS page and robots.txt are both behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (confirmed live, HTTP 403), so I could not read the actual terms. Scoped to metadata-only, no file mirroring, flagged in its own header for human sign-off. 7. **Weekly refresh** — `deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.{timer,service}` + `scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh`, following the exact existing `nxeon-nightly-scan` pattern. Not installed. **Critical: a security review I commissioned mid-task found two real bugs in my new renderer before I considered it done** — a stored-XSS attribute break-out (URLs embedded in `src=`/`href=` without escaping) and a ReDoS (110 seconds to hang the render on a 5,990-char adversarial string). Both fixed and re-verified with the exact repro strings (0-1ms now, no break-out). A separate, **pre-existing, out-of-scope** JSON-LD script-injection bug was found in the same review (untouched by my diff) — spun off as a separate background task. **Real production numbers** (`GameMod`, active+upstreamOk, 45,761 rows): catalogue-wide `longDescription` coverage went **5.1% → 74.6%**; Modrinth alone **0% → 98.8%** (31,842/32,243 rows). **What ran against production:** only `scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts` (unmodified, pre-existing script) — dry-run → 50-row apply → eyeballed real rendered pages → full 32,193-row run. All other code (renderer, importer fixes, uMod importer, weekly timer) is **uncommitted** in the worktree — not pushed (this repo auto-pushes on commit) — staged for human review. **Needs a human call:** uMod ToS, the ~400-row (1.2%) Modrinth batch that consistently 400s (not yet root-caused, script is idempotent/safe to retry later), and the JSON-LD fix I spun off. Full writeup with all details: `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new dated section at the end) and `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc/ROADMAP.md`. result: NxLabs mod-description gap fixed — Modrinth/Steam/Thunderstore/uMod importer + renderer fixes staged for review in `/opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc` (branch `fix/nxlabs-mod-descriptions`, uncommitted), with the mandated Modrinth backfill run for real against production (catalogue-wide description coverage 5.1%→74.6%), and two real security bugs (stored XSS, ReDoS) found and fixed in the new renderer before shipping.
